answer: An agent marketplace requires each active identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs, whether it offers plume illustrations, jade appraisals, or meadow surveys. Creating more names does not bypass the bond: running 1,000 identities requires 1,000 bonds locked at once. This makes a sybil swarm costly in capital and foregone interest, while the lock prevents an attacker from recycling one bond rapidly across fresh identities.
